evidence.excerpt: Personalised pricing—setting individual rates based on inferred consumer willingness to pay—offers revenue managers potentially large gains but conflicts with European data protection rules under the GDPR. This paper develops a formal model of constrained personalised pricing in which the hotel revenue manager maximises expected revenue subject to a data minimisation constraint that limits the number of consumer attributes usable in rate discrimination. The model is parameterised using conjoint survey data from 502 hotel guests in four countries (Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Austria) and solved numerically. Results show that even a two-attribute rate model (trip purpose, booking channel) recovers 61% of the theoretical full-information revenue gain, while satisfying a plausible interpretation of GDPR data minimisation. The study offers a practical framework that legal and revenue management departments can use jointly to design compliant personalisation strategies.
